sentences.text:
ORDER Learned counsel for respondent No. 1/State informed that notice has been duly served on respondent No. 2.
2. Case Diary is available.

3. This first criminal appeal has been filed under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (in short "Act, 1989") against the order dated 30.06.2025 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities Act), Vidisha, rejecting the regular bail application of the appellant.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. The appellant has been arrested on 05.02.2025 in connection with Crime No.79/2025 registered at Police Station - Dehat, District Vidisha (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376 and 506 of IPC and Sections 3(2)(va), 3(1)(w-ii), 3(2)(v) of the Act, 1989.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28123 2 CRA-10469-2025 5.

Prosecution story, in short, is that on 12.04.2024 at about 04:30 PM, present appellant took the prosecutrix with him on a motorcycle towards bypass and took her in a room and committed rape Atul Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172036310/
1 upon her.

sentences.text: When prosecutrix objected then he has threatened her for life and when the marriage of prosecutrix was fixed then appellant had made her video viral, due to which, her marriage was broken.
Prosecutrix has lodged the FIR after four months' delay.
Accordingly, the offence has been registered.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the matter.
He is in custody since 05.02.2026.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix is major, matured and married lady.

FIR is four months'
delayed.
Semen was not found on the panty of the prosecutrix.
No DNA has been conducted.
Final conclusion of trial will take long time.
Hence, he prays that the appellant may be enlarged on bail.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the criminal appeal and prays for its rejection by submitting that video is available in the matter.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
9.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also taking note of the fact that the investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed, appellant is suffering jail incarceration since last about 9 months, prosecutrix is major and matured lady, FIR is four months' delayed, and final conclusion of trial will take long time, I deem it proper to grant bail to the appellant.

Accordingly,
without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28123 3 CRA-10469-2025 criminal appeal is allowed and impugned order dated 30.06.2025 is hereby set aside.
10.

It is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C/480(3) of BNSS.
11.
With the aforesaid, present criminal appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
12. Certified Copy as per rules.
